blocks.x: Job matching rebuilt on a skills spine — placement rate up 18% and counselor caseload time redirected to the hard-to-place
Identity withheld — an employment agency matching people to vacancies by keyword while the labor market moved to skills. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter measured the keyword gap: placement rate 22% below European peers, counselors spending 68% of caseload time on administratively easy matches, and the hard-to-place — career changers, gap resumes — effectively invisible to the keyword engine.
Vacancy postings described skills; candidate profiles described job titles. The translation happened by accident in a counselor's head, or not at all.

We built the skills spine: vacancy and candidate profiles normalized to one skills model with equivalences the agency's counselors curate, match rankings produced with the reasoning exposed — which skills, which gaps, which bridges — counselor queues ranked by need rather than ease, and outcome tracking scoring the matching continuously. The easy matches automated; the hard ones got the humans.
